# Implementation Plan: agent-tree-rpc

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-13. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/agent-tree-rpc/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Expose codex's live in-process agent spawn tree as a queryable + streamable RPC surface that mobile clients (happy-app) can render. Codex already maintains the data internally (`AgentRegistry.agent_tree` in `codex-rs/core/src/agent/registry.rs`) and emits `CollabAgentSpawnBegin/EndEvent` plus the v2 `ThreadItem::CollabAgentToolCall` items, but nothing on the Node side parses those events into a unified tree representation. This task adds the bridge entirely on the happy-cli side (no codex submodule edits per the minimize-conflict-surface tenet), plus the small server-side socket-typing + fan-out extension required to deliver a new `agent-tree-update` Socket.IO frame.

Two RPC shapes:
1. `sessionGetAgentTree(sessionId)` (CLI-registered session RPC) → `{ nodes: AgentTreeNode[], edges: { parent, child }[], seq: number }` snapshot.
2. `agent-tree-update` Socket.IO event — incremental deltas (`pending-spawn-started | node-added | node-status-changed | node-removed`) with a monotonic `seq` so reconnecting clients can RPC for a snapshot and then forward-apply deltas without race.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
- Monorepo: pnpm workspace, TypeScript 5.9, Vitest, Socket.IO 4.x, Fastify 5.
- `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts:586-691` already holds a long-lived `client.setEventHandler((msg) => {...})` per session — this is the correct hook for tree maintenance.
- `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts` — v2 `item/*` notifications are parsed in **`handleRawNotification` starting at line 324** (NOT in `handleNotification` at line 1701, which only dispatches to `handleRawNotification` first then falls through to legacy `codex/event`). Today the function has explicit cases for `commandExecution`, `fileChange`, `agentMessage`, but no case for `item.type === 'collabAgentToolCall'` — that item falls through `return method.startsWith('item/')` at line 460 and is silently consumed. This is where the spawn-event parser must go.
- The legacy `codex/event` path is still active. `CollabAgentSpawnBegin` / `CollabAgentSpawnEndEvent` reach `eventHandler` through that path today, even before v2 wiring lands. The reducer must therefore dedup spawn events by `(callId, phase)` so the same begin/end is not double-counted when both streams emit.
- `runCodex.ts` uses the existing `session.rpcHandlerManager.registerHandler('abort', handleAbort)` pattern (see the existing call in `runCodex.ts:501`) for new RPC registration. happy-server's generic `rpcHandler.ts` routes `${sessionId}:sessionGetAgentTree` automatically. No new RPC handler file on the server.
- `packages/happy-server/sources/app/events/eventRouter.ts` only emits `update` / `ephemeral` Socket.IO frames today. The existing `emitUpdate` / `emitEphemeral` signatures (file lines 242–253) BOTH take `{ userId, payload, recipientFilter }` — `userId` is mandatory because Socket.IO rooms are `user:${userId}:session:${sessionId}` (see file lines 281–286). Any new emit method must follow the same shape.
- happy-server runs **embedded single-user per daemon process** (per `packages/happy-server/CLAUDE.md` "Architecture posture"); `userId` plumbing is still required (do not strip ad-hoc), but in practice each EventRouter instance only serves one user.
- `packages/happy-wire/` is the shared Zod / type contract package consumed by both happy-cli and happy-server. New `AgentTreeNode` / `AgentTreeDelta` schemas live here so both ends typecheck against the same source.
- Codex v2 item `CollabAgentToolCall` (in `codex/external/repos/.../app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs`) carries threadId + status but NOT nickname/role/lastTaskMessage. Nickname + role can be recovered from the legacy `codex/event` payload (still flowing) or from a follow-up `thread/read`. `lastTaskMessage` is not exposed by the app-server protocol; the plan adopts best-effort derivation.

### Technical Constraints
- **Codex submodule is READ-ONLY** (`plans/codexu-roadmap.md` minimize-conflict-surface tenet). All Node-side work only.
- **The "watch::Receiver" pitfall**: Codex's Rust `subscribe_status(agent_id) -> watch::Receiver<AgentStatus>` (in `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control.rs:~832`) cannot be held directly by Node. The Node-side analog is the existing JSON-RPC notification stream on `CodexAppServerClient` — that stream must remain subscribed across the entire codex session lifetime. The bug pattern to avoid: re-registering the event handler inside a per-turn / per-tool callback, which would silently drop spawn events after the first turn.
- **Spawn-begin has no child threadId** — only `call_id` + `sender_thread_id` (parent) are known. The delta union must include a `pending-spawn-started` variant so the acceptance assertion of "ordered begin and end deltas per child with parent linkage" is verifiable. `node-added` (with the real child `threadId`) only emits on spawn-end.
- **Socket fan-out is currently 2-kind** (update/ephemeral). Adding a third frame is a cross-package socket contract change covering `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket.ts` and `packages/happy-cli/src/api/types.ts`.
- **Replay vs snapshot**: only `emitUpdate(...)` is replayed by happy-server. `agent-tree-update` is transient — clients always RPC for the snapshot on mount/reconnect, then forward-apply deltas (sequence-numbered, monotonic).
- **Build order**: `happy-wire` compiles before `happy-cli` / `happy-server` (already wired via `workspace:*` deps in their `package.json`).

## Approach

### Architecture

```
codex (Rust)                    happy-cli (Node)                 happy-server                 happy-app (future)
─────────────                   ────────────────                 ─────────────                ─────────────────
AgentRegistry.agent_tree
CollabAgentSpawnBegin/End  ──►  CodexAppServerClient
                                  handleNotification +
                                  setEventHandler  ───────────►  RPC route:
                                AgentTreeState                     ${sessionId}:sessionGetAgentTree ◄── snapshot RPC
                                  (pure reducer +                Socket.IO frame:
                                   in-memory cache)                'agent-tree-update'    ◄── delta stream
                                  emits delta ◄── runCodex
                                  registers RPC
                                  on session start

                                runCodex.handleKillSession:
                                  state.clear()
                                  unregister RPC
```

- Single-writer ordering: `setEventHandler` callback is invoked sequentially by `CodexAppServerClient`; reducer mutates cache synchronously and emits the delta in the same step. No queueing.
- Snapshot ↔ stream race: every snapshot response carries `seq`; every delta carries `seq`. Clients hold `appliedSeq` and ignore deltas with `seq <= appliedSeq`.
- Per-session lifetime: `AgentTreeState` is created in `runCodex.ts` BEFORE `client.setEventHandler(...)` so the handler can write into it on the very first event (the handler does not fire until `client.connect()` succeeds, but initialization before registration is the simpler invariant), and torn down in `handleKillSession`. NOT a singleton.

### Implementation Strategy

Implement in this order so each step compiles and tests independently:

1. **Shared wire types** (`packages/happy-wire/`) — define `AgentTreeNode`, `AgentTreeEdge`, `AgentTreeSnapshot`, `AgentTreeDelta` union, and the RPC + Socket.IO payload schemas (Zod). Re-export from `packages/happy-wire/src/index.ts`.
2. **Pure reducer** (`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/agentTreeState.ts`) — closed-over state with two maps (`nodes` by threadId, `pendingByCallId`) and a monotonic `seq` counter. Public surface: `applyEvent(evt) -> AgentTreeDelta[]` (array, possibly empty — required because `closeAgent` may emit multiple `node-removed` deltas in one event for the closed subtree; ordering is "descendants first, then explicit target"; each delta in the array carries its own incremented `seq`), `snapshot() -> AgentTreeSnapshot`, `clear()`. Colocated vitest exhaustively covers the reducer.
3. **Codex v2 parser extension** (`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts`) — add a case in **`handleRawNotification` (line ~324)** for `item.type === 'collabAgentToolCall'` that decodes the begin/end/state payload into a typed `AgentTreeEvent` and forwards it to the existing `setEventHandler` callback. Preserve `params.threadId` (camelCase — v2 wire is camelCase; existing tests use `threadId`) on emitted `agent_message` events so the reducer can update `lastTaskMessage` for the right child. Keep the legacy `codex/event` path emitting `collab_agent_spawn_begin` / `collab_agent_spawn_end` (snake_case — `codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs` uses `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`) working — both flows feed the same reducer, which **deduplicates by `(callId, phase)`** so a spawn observed on both wire formats only mutates the tree once. Reducer also reads `node-status-changed` / `node-removed` from v2 `CollabAgentToolCall.tool` variants (`sendInput`, `wait`, `closeAgent`, `resumeAgent`) plus their legacy snake_case counterparts.
4. **CLI socket typing** (`packages/happy-cli/src/api/types.ts`) — declare the `agent-tree-update` event on the `ClientToServerEvents` map (CLI inbound to server is `{ delta }`) AND on the `ServerToClientEvents` map (server outbound to clients is `{ sessionId, delta }`). This is where the cross-package typed contract actually lives; `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket.ts` uses untyped Socket.IO `Server`/`Socket` and only needs payload-validation changes, not a typed surface extension. **Typing must land before Step 5** so the helper's `socket.emit('agent-tree-update', { delta })` typechecks.
5. **CLI session helper** (`packages/happy-cli/src/api/apiSession.ts`) — add `sendAgentTreeUpdate(delta)` that emits the typed Socket.IO frame `agent-tree-update` with payload `{ delta }` (NO `sessionId` field) over the existing per-session socket. The server derives the authoritative `sessionId` from `connection.sessionId` (the session-scoped connection identity), not from the client payload. This eliminates the spoof vector AND keeps the inbound wire payload minimal. The OUTBOUND frame the server sends to clients carries `{ sessionId, delta }` so user-scoped subscribers (which receive events for multiple sessions) can demultiplex.
6. **Runtime wiring** (`packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.ts`) — construct `AgentTreeState` **before** calling `client.setEventHandler(...)` (state must exist when the handler fires); in the event handler dispatch spawn / status events into the reducer, forward each emitted delta via `sendAgentTreeUpdate`; register `sessionGetAgentTree` RPC using the same `session.rpcHandlerManager.registerHandler(...)` pattern that `runCodex.ts:501` uses for `abort`. Clear state + unregister the RPC in `handleKillSession` (`runCodex.ts:465-498`).
7. **Server payload typing** (Zod schemas in `packages/happy-wire`) — incoming CLI `agent-tree-update` frame is validated server-side using the same Zod schema defined in step 1. No separate "server socket typing" file is touched.
8. **Server inbound handler** (`packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket/sessionUpdateHandler.ts`) — receive the CLI `agent-tree-update` frame; **authorize: reject unless `connection.connectionType === 'session-scoped'`** (this prevents a user-scoped or machine-scoped socket from emitting deltas at all). The authoritative `sessionId` is read from `connection.sessionId` — the client payload does NOT carry `sessionId`, so spoofing into a different session is impossible by construction. Validate the `{ delta }` payload with the Zod schema from happy-wire; call `eventRouter.emitAgentTreeUpdate({ userId, sessionId: connection.sessionId, delta })`.
9. **Server fan-out** (`packages/happy-server/sources/app/events/eventRouter.ts`) — add `emitAgentTreeUpdate({ userId, sessionId, delta })` whose signature mirrors the existing `emitUpdate` / `emitEphemeral` shape (file lines 242–253), using `recipientFilter: { type: 'all-interested-in-session', sessionId }`. The room resolution at file lines 372–380 already fans out `all-interested-in-session` to BOTH `user:${userId}:session:${sessionId}` AND `user:${userId}:user-scoped`. The outbound Socket.IO frame carries `{ sessionId, delta }` (server adds the trusted `sessionId`) so user-scoped subscribers can demultiplex events that span multiple sessions. Do NOT add to the replay buffer — clients re-RPC `sessionGetAgentTree` on reconnect. **Widen** `RoutedSocketEvent.eventName` and the `publish` / `emitToLocalSink` / `EventRouter` interface unions from `'update' | 'ephemeral'` to also include `'agent-tree-update'`; update any typed test fakes (`createFakeEventRouter()` in `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket.spec.ts` if it exists). Colocated vitest in `eventRouter.test.ts` (existing file uses `.test.ts` naming despite the project convention `.spec.ts`; mirror the existing test file).
10. **Test coverage** — Layer-1 rule (`packages/happy-cli/agents.md`): `codex.integration.test.ts` must exercise the real codex CLI surface; mocked tests do not count as primary acceptance.
   - **Primary acceptance** lives in `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codex.integration.test.ts` as a new long-form test guarded by the existing `RUN_CODEX_INTEGRATION === "1"` env gate. The existing harness in that file drives a real `codex app-server` through `CodexAppServerClient` directly but does NOT boot `runCodex.ts` end-to-end. The new test therefore mounts an in-test bridge: it constructs the production `AgentTreeState` reducer, hands the CodexAppServerClient's `setEventHandler` callback through the same dispatch the production `runCodex.ts` will use, and captures emitted deltas through a fake `sendAgentTreeUpdate` sink (this is the unit-of-test seam — the **real** codex sub-process is still on the other end of the wire, satisfying the "real CLI" intent). The test prompts the real codex to spawn 2 sub-agents (child A under root, child B under A), asserts the captured deltas as an **ordered subsequence** (spawn deltas appear in the asserted order, but additional status deltas may interleave — the test must tolerate them rather than require exact equality, because the live model may emit additional `node-status-changed` events), and asserts the final `state.snapshot()` topology.
   - **runCodex glue test** (NEW, mirrors existing `runCodex.fork.test.ts` / `runCodexPublishMode.test.ts` / `runCodex.attachmentsIgnore.test.ts`): in `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.agentTree.test.ts`, feed a controlled `CodexAppServerClient` event into the production `runCodex` boot path and assert (a) `sessionGetAgentTree` RPC is registered on the session's `rpcHandlerManager` after `client.connect()`, (b) calling that registered RPC returns a snapshot matching the reducer state, (c) an incoming spawn-begin event causes a `sendAgentTreeUpdate` invocation, and (d) `handleKillSession` unregisters the RPC and clears state. This is the test that catches the "forgot to wire it in `runCodex`" regression.
   - **Support coverage**: `agentTreeState.test.ts` (pure reducer, synthetic events) covers reducer correctness exhaustively including dedup, monotonic seq across array-returning `applyEvent`, and the `closeAgent` subtree-removal case (multiple `node-removed` deltas in one call, descendants-first order).
   - **CodexAppServerClient parser case** is covered by a colocated `.test.ts` on `codexAppServerClient.ts` that feeds a synthetic `item/started` / `item/completed` for `collabAgentToolCall` and asserts the emitted typed event shape, including preservation of `params.threadId` (camelCase — matches existing v2 wire) so the reducer can update `lastTaskMessage` on subsequent `agent_message` items for the right child.
   - **Authorization test** lives in a new `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket/sessionUpdateHandler.test.ts` that asserts a non-session-scoped connection's `agent-tree-update` emission is rejected and not forwarded to `eventRouter`.
11. **Docs** — Update `plans/agent-view-research.md` §6 `agent-tree-rpc` row inline with a "Delivered (branch <branch-name>)" marker (no SHA — `plans/codexu-roadmap.md:5-9` requires that any roadmap-affecting commit also refresh `plans/overview.html`, and a self-referencing SHA cannot be in the same commit). Update `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` recent-deliveries / Phase status section with a one-line entry. Update `plans/parallel-assignments.md` task entry (line ~372) and status table row (line ~566) from "🟡 in progress" to "✅ done"; verify the downstream `agent-status-stream` guidance (line ~427) is consistent with the wire semantics this plan ships. **Regenerate `plans/overview.html` in the same commit** per the markdown-authoritative/HTML-derivative rule in `plans/codexu-roadmap.md:5-9`.

## Scope

### In Scope
- New shared types in `happy-wire` for agent-tree node/edge/snapshot/delta.
- happy-cli reducer + state holder for the spawn tree.
- happy-cli v2 protocol parser extension for `collabAgentToolCall` items.
- happy-cli session RPC registration: `sessionGetAgentTree`.
- happy-cli emission of `agent-tree-update` Socket.IO frames per delta, with monotonic `seq`.
- happy-server typed socket surface extension for `agent-tree-update`.
- happy-server fan-out (`emitAgentTreeUpdate`) to all clients in the session room.
- Pure-reducer vitest in happy-cli.
- Fan-out vitest in happy-server.
- End-to-end ordering + parent-linkage vitest in happy-cli.
- Doc updates in `plans/agent-view-research.md` and `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`.
- Single commit on `main`.

### Out of Scope
- Any change under `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` (Rust submodule).
- Mobile UI (`packages/happy-app/sources/app/(app)/session/[id]/agents.tsx`) consumption — flagged as a future follow-up; not in this commit.
- Replay/persistence of agent-tree state in happy-server's DB. Clients re-RPC on reconnect.
- Authoritative `lastTaskMessage` (codex app-server doesn't expose it). Field is optional in the wire schema; CLI populates best-effort from spawn prompt + observed `agent_message` items.
- Cross-session aggregation. Each session owns its own tree.

## Risk Areas

1. **Receiver-lifetime regression** (the explicit pitfall). Mitigation: single registration of the event handler in `runCodex.ts` (state initialized BEFORE `setEventHandler`, NOT after `client.connect()` — the existing flow in `runCodex.ts` registers the handler before connect); teardown only in `handleKillSession`. Code review gate: grep for new `setEventHandler` calls anywhere outside `runCodex` boot.
2. **Spawn-begin has no threadId.** Mitigation: dedicated `pending-spawn-started` delta variant keyed by `callId`; reducer resolves to `node-added` on spawn-end. Test asserts the 4-delta ordered sequence.
3. **Snapshot/stream race on reconnect.** Mitigation: monotonic `seq` on both snapshot and deltas; client applies `delta.seq > appliedSeq` only. Defined in the wire schema and asserted in reducer tests.
4. **Cross-package typecheck.** Mitigation: implement in dependency order (wire → cli/server consumers); CI runs `pnpm build` at the end of the implementation.
5. **`collabAgentToolCall` parser silently broken.** Mitigation: parser case lives in `handleRawNotification` (line ~324) alongside the existing `commandExecution` / `fileChange` / `agentMessage` cases; explicit unit case in `codexAppServerClient.test.ts` for the v2 item shape; failure to parse fails the test.
5a. **Double-counted spawns** if legacy `codex/event` and v2 `collabAgentToolCall` both fire for the same spawn. Mitigation: reducer dedups by `(callId, phase)`; covered by AC2.
5b. **Spoofed deltas** — without authorization, any authenticated socket could emit `agent-tree-update` frames. Mitigation: server inbound handler rejects unless `connectionType === 'session-scoped'`, and the trusted `sessionId` is read from `connection.sessionId` (set at socket-auth time in `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket.ts:71`), never from the client payload. Note: this guarantees a session-scoped connection can only emit deltas for ITS OWN session, but does not prevent an authenticated client that legitimately holds a `session-scoped` connection from emitting deltas for that session. Under the single-user embedded-daemon threat model (`packages/happy-server/CLAUDE.md` "Architecture posture"), only the user's own CLI process holds a session-scoped connection, so this is sufficient. Covered by AC4b.
6. **`lastTaskMessage` always empty** (not exposed by app-server). Documented as optional; not asserted in acceptance test; future codex-side enhancement tracked separately.
7. **Memory leak on long sessions.** Mitigation: explicit `state.clear()` in `handleKillSession` before `client.disconnect()`. State is bounded by live-agent count (<100 typical).
8. **Event-handler ordering perturbation.** Mitigation: reducer is synchronous; delta emission is synchronous in the same callback step. No `setImmediate` / `Promise.resolve().then(...)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Cross-package typecheck is green for the three packages this change touches: `pnpm --filter @slopus/happy-wire build && pnpm --filter happy build && pnpm --filter happy-server build` (the repo root has no `build` script, so a bare `pnpm build` is wrong; use either the per-package filters here or `pnpm -r build` if a full workspace build is desired). On Windows / Git Bash run with `npm_config_script_shell=bash` prepended.
- [ ] AC2: happy-cli reducer vitest (`agentTreeState.test.ts`) passes: ordered begin/end events produce a snapshot with two child nodes + correct edges + monotonic seq; `(callId, phase)` dedup is verified by feeding the same begin twice and asserting only one delta is emitted.
- [ ] AC3: happy-server fan-out vitest (`eventRouter.test.ts`) passes: an `emitAgentTreeUpdate({ userId, sessionId, delta })` call delivers the `agent-tree-update` frame (outbound payload **`{ sessionId, delta }` — the trusted `sessionId` is added by the server**, so user-scoped subscribers receiving events for multiple sessions can demultiplex) to a `FakeSocket` joined to room `user:${userId}:session:${sessionId}` AND to a `FakeSocket` joined to `user:${userId}:user-scoped` (this matches the current `all-interested-in-session` routing in `eventRouter.ts:372-380` which fans out to both rooms), and does NOT deliver to a `FakeSocket` joined only to `user:${userId}:machine:${otherMachineId}`. Inbound `agent-tree-update` from the CLI side, by contrast, must NOT carry `sessionId` — that is the spoofing-prevention contract.
- [ ] AC4 (primary acceptance, per `packages/happy-cli/agents.md`): happy-cli `codex.integration.test.ts` passes a new long-form test that uses the **real** codex CLI to spawn 2 sub-agents (child A under root, child B under child A); the test wires production `AgentTreeState` to the same `CodexAppServerClient.setEventHandler` callback `runCodex.ts` uses and captures the emitted deltas through a fake `sendAgentTreeUpdate` sink. The test asserts the captured deltas contain the **ordered subsequence** `pending-spawn-started(A) → node-added(A) → pending-spawn-started(B) → node-added(B)` (extra interleaved `node-status-changed` deltas are tolerated; the seq values must be strictly increasing across the captured stream); `state.snapshot()` returns a topology with `nodes` containing exactly A and B (root is intentionally excluded per `AgentRegistry.live_agents()` semantics) and `edges` `[{parent: rootThreadId, child: A.threadId}, {parent: A.threadId, child: B.threadId}]`. Run with `RUN_CODEX_INTEGRATION=1 npm_config_script_shell=bash pnpm --filter happy exec vitest run src/codex/codex.integration.test.ts` — without the env var the gated test is skipped and AC4 is NOT considered met. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or equivalent codex auth credential) in the environment. The test must use deterministic prompts (e.g., "spawn one explorer named A and instruct A to spawn one explorer named B") and a per-spawn timeout (≤120s) to bound model nondeterminism.
- [ ] AC4a (support, parser): `codexAppServerClient.test.ts` covers the new `collabAgentToolCall` branch with synthetic v2 notifications and verifies `params.threadId` (camelCase) is preserved on emitted `agent_message` events (so the reducer can update `lastTaskMessage` for the correct child).
- [ ] AC4b (support, authorization): new `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket/sessionUpdateHandler.test.ts` (or extension of an existing test file in that directory) asserts that an `agent-tree-update` frame from a `connectionType !== 'session-scoped'` connection is dropped and does NOT reach `eventRouter`.
- [ ] AC4c (support, runCodex glue): new `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.agentTree.test.ts` (NOT gated by `RUN_CODEX_INTEGRATION`; uses a controlled CodexAppServerClient stand-in) asserts (i) `sessionGetAgentTree` is registered on the session's `rpcHandlerManager` after boot, (ii) calling that registered RPC returns a snapshot matching the in-memory reducer, (iii) a synthesized spawn-begin event flowing through the real `setEventHandler` callback triggers `sendAgentTreeUpdate`, (iv) `handleKillSession` unregisters the RPC and clears state. This test exists specifically to catch a "forgot to wire the feature in `runCodex`" regression that AC2/AC4a/AC4b would all miss.
- [ ] AC5: No file under `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` is modified. Because `codex/` is a git submodule (per `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`), the parent-repo `git diff --name-only -- codex/external/repos/codex-patched` only sees the submodule pointer, not its internal worktree. Verify pre-commit with the submodule-aware combination: `git -C codex diff --name-only -- external/repos/codex-patched` (must return empty) AND `git diff --submodule=diff -- codex` (must report no content delta inside the submodule). Both must be clean.
- [ ] AC6: The change lands as a single commit on `main`.
- [ ] AC7: `plans/agent-view-research.md` §6 `agent-tree-rpc` row is updated to "Delivered (branch <branch-name>)" — no SHA (a commit cannot contain its own SHA).
- [ ] AC8: `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` recent-deliveries section gets a one-line entry referencing this work.
- [ ] AC9: `plans/overview.html` is regenerated from the updated markdown in the same commit (per `plans/codexu-roadmap.md:5-9` markdown-authoritative / HTML-derivative rule).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

See `stories-outline.md` for the full breakdown. Summary:

1. **US-001** — Shared wire types (`happy-wire/src/agentTree.ts`)
2. **US-002** — Pure reducer + unit test (`agentTreeState.ts` + `.test.ts`)
3. **US-003** — Codex v2 parser extension in `codexAppServerClient.ts`
4. **US-004** — CLI runtime wiring in `runCodex.ts` + apiSession helper + types
5. **US-005** — Server socket typing + fan-out (`socket.ts`, `eventRouter.ts`, `sessionUpdateHandler.ts`, fan-out test)
6. **US-006** — End-to-end integration test (`codex.integration.test.ts`)
7. **US-007** — Doc updates (`plans/agent-view-research.md`, `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`)

## Open Questions

- None blocking. Design decisions documented inline:
  - **`lastTaskMessage`** — codex app-server protocol does not expose this field today. Strategy: derive an initial value from the spawn-begin prompt; subsequent observed `agent_message` items on the child thread update the field. The wire schema marks the field optional and the acceptance test does NOT assert on it. (Future codex-side enhancement to expose `AgentMetadata.last_task_message` via the app-server protocol is tracked separately.)
  - **Spawn-begin has no child threadId** — emit `pending-spawn-started` keyed by `callId`; `node-added` emits only on spawn-end with the real child `threadId`. The 4-delta ordering (`pending-A, added-A, pending-B, added-B`) is what AC4 asserts.
  - **`closeAgent` subtree semantics** — codex's `closeAgent` in `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control.rs` closes the target AND its live descendants. The reducer therefore must remove the closed node AND all descendants tracked in its local `nodes` map; it emits one `node-removed` per node (descendants first, then the explicit target). The reducer test covers this case.
  - **Nickname / role** — v2 `CollabAgentToolCall` does NOT carry these fields; legacy `collab_agent_spawn_end` does (`new_agent_nickname`, `new_agent_role` per `codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`). Strategy for THIS commit: legacy-event best-effort; if only v2 is observed, leave both fields null. A `thread/read` follow-up (which would require a new `ThreadReadParams` / `ThreadReadResponse` typed helper in `codexAppServerClient.ts` + handler plumbing) is **explicitly deferred** — adding it here would expand scope beyond the single-commit constraint. AC4 asserts nickname + role are populated on the real-codex path because legacy is still emitted today; if the codex protocol drops legacy events in the future, this AC must be loosened to "field may be null" rather than adding the thread/read helper in a rushed amendment.
  - **Dedup vs metadata merge** — when both v2 and legacy spawn-end arrive for the same `(callId, phase)`, the reducer emits only one structural delta (dedup) but MAY merge the richer metadata (nickname/role from legacy) into the existing node WITHOUT producing an additional delta. The reducer test covers: (1) v2-first then legacy-second → final snapshot has legacy nickname/role; (2) legacy-first then v2-second → no information loss; (3) repeated identical event → no node mutation and no second delta.
  - **Distinct frame vs reusing `ephemeral`** — the plan adds a third `agent-tree-update` Socket.IO frame rather than tunneling deltas through the existing `ephemeral` frame. Trade-off: a distinct frame is clearer for the client (no payload-type discrimination on the receive side) at the cost of a one-time socket-contract extension in `packages/happy-cli/src/api/types.ts`. The single-user embedded-daemon posture (per `packages/happy-server/CLAUDE.md` Architecture posture) makes this contract change low-risk.
